newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan mulls seconding more staff to Automakers.
newsitem.headline: Nissan mulls seconding more staff to Automakers.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Monday it is considering seconding more staff to Automakers Ltd of South Africa.
Nissan said on Friday it would acquire 50 percent of Automakers for 360.75 million rand on July 1 to boost output and sales in the South African market.
A Nissan spokeswoman said the firm is considering seconding Nissan executives and sales and production staff to the South African firm and hopes to finalise details by July 1.
Four Nissan engineers currently support production at the South African carmaker and the Nissan employs another 12 people at its representative office there.
Sales of Nissan cars in South Africa fell to 34,000 units in calendar 1996 from 42,000 a year earlier due to a lack of new models.
The spokeswomen said the overall South African car market is expected to grow to 500,000 units by the year 2000 from 380,000 in 1996.
